title: Re-recording: mother, the flood and the 1910 census
summary: Helen Dance restarts the lost tape; Durham recalls a flood before 1910 and a census listing parents Rabb and Joseph Durham and the children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Eddie, this is Helen, and we are going to go back and do some of that material we did earlier which turned out to be abortive because of the tape. So now we have to hope that everything's going well and we can remember all those interesting things we were talking about.
I do remember what we started out with. We started out talking about your mother being a schoolteacher.
In San Marcos, and then we got to the flood --
-- which we said was the Rio Grande, wasn't it? And it was in about -- did you say 1908?
Had to be around about that, because it was just a little before '10. It was before the --
And the reason you remember that is because the records of 1910 --
It's the only time they took the inventory of the state.
And they sent me a copy of it. This was in 1910 and that was so many children born to Rabb. She was a Rabb.

And they named them -- as far as they got it, it was Joe, Earl and Edward and Roosevelt. They didn't know -- and there was one child born the same time, another child born and they thought that there was born in so and so, and they named off the children, but they wasn't sure about the time they was born, but what they had found.
And that was from 1910, I believe. They didn't have nothing before '10.
They took a census and that came from Baltimore, Maryland, I think, or somewhere, or Texas someplace. I don't know. They got it from someplace.
